newsitem.title: HONG KONG: WEEK AHEAD-HK stocks still vulnerable - analysts.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD-HK stocks still vulnerable - analysts.

text.p: Hong Kong's stocks could slide further before buying begins after a shakeout last week pummeled the Hang Seng Index to a two-month low, analysts said.

The blue-chip index fell 547.24 points, or 4.01 percent, to end at 13,113.26 on Friday in the biggest weekly point decline since March 1996. The index also hit a low of 12,962.15 on Friday, its lowest level since December 19.
"The market is actually entering a corrective stage. Over the next few weeks, I think the market will test 12,750," said Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities.
The Hang Seng's failure to push above 14,000 points had led some investors to take profits in Hong Kong and shift their focus to other markets that offered value, analysts said.
The Hang Seng Index hit an all-time high of 14,004.93 on January 16.
"People are fully invested in Hong Kong and looking to other markets. People are chasing the run-away train on Wall Street," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at Nava SC Securities.
The Dow industrials rose above 7,000 points for the first time last week.
Analysts said Wall Street could be nearing a correction that could also weigh on the local market in the week ahead.
"Obviously, New York is going to be due for a correction. That will unsettle trading here," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
Kelvin Tang, an analyst at ImPac Asset Management, said domestic factors were also hurting the Hong Kong market.
"There is poor sentiment towards property developers. We have to see some positive news to trigger some more buying interest," he said.
Tang said activity should pick up in the week ahead after the slow return from the Chinese New Year holiday last week.
"Maybe next week we can see the real big picture of the Hong Kong market," he added.
Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities, was expecting some stabilisation in the coming week. "It seems that Hong Kong stocks have been quite oversold in the near term."
He said the Hang Seng Index could move in a range of 13,000 to 13,600 in the week ahead.
"It seems to me that 13,000 is the first support for the market and there is very good support at 12,500," said Percy Au-Young, director of research at DBS Securities.
He said investors would look for bargains below 13,000.
"There will be some bargain-hunting at lower levels in anticipation of a recovery in March," said Kwong.
Upcoming earnings reports could pleasantly surprise, leading to a pick-up in interest, analysts said.
"Earnings results should be well above consensus estimates so, therefore, it should stage a rebound," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International.
Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels Ltd is due to report its final results on Wednesday.
On Monday, the Hong Kong Legislative Council is to discuss a report by China Light & Power Co Ltd on the costs of deferring construction at its Black Point power station.
